notes.title: Lacuna turns 4 – and what a journey it's been!
notes.notes:
Fellow Detectives!

Hard to believe, but it’s already been four years since [i]Lacuna[/i] first launched—and it’s still going strong. Earlier this year, we quietly passed 300,000 copies sold across all platforms, and we’re beyond grateful for everyone who’s joined Neil on his story so far. 💙

As if that milestone wasn’t special enough, we also had the incredible honor of hearing part of [i]Lacuna[/i]’s soundtrack brought to life by a live orchestra once again. For us, the soundtrack wasn’t just background, it was a true passion project, composed by Julian Colbus (one of our own team members). And let us tell you: nothing quite compares to the feeling of hearing your own music played by real musicians.

[b]Here's a short snippet of the live concert:[/b]

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q-3IYB5xUPs

From the bottom of our hearts, thank you for supporting [i]Lacuna[/i], sharing your thoughts, and spreading the word over the years. You’ve made this adventure unforgettable.

[b]🎉 Happy anniversary, Lacuna! 🎻[/b]

And while we have you here: if you enjoyed [i]Lacuna[/i], make sure to check out our second title, [b]Between Horizons[/b]! It’s been out for over a year now and continues the spirit of meaningful sci-fi storytelling and branching narratives. The soundtrack? Crafted by the same composer who poured his heart into [i]Lacuna[/i]. 💫

[b]Thanks for sticking with us. Here’s to many more stories to come![/b]

notes.title: Next Sci-Fi Detective Adventure From The Creators of Lacuna!
notes.notes:
Hey, everybody!

This is DigiTales Interactive, creators of Lacuna. If you liked our first game, we thought you might be interested in this announcement: Today, we and our publisher Assemble Entertainment proudly announce our upcoming second title, [b]Between Horizons[/b]!

[h2]What Is It?[/h2]

Between Horizons is a [b]story-driven detective game[/b] set aboard the [b]semi-open world[/b] of a [b]generation ship[/b] en route to another star. You assume the role of Stella, the ship's young Chief of Security, who is faced with multiple problems threatening to jeopardize the mission. You will have to make some [b]tough moral choices[/b] and [b]think hard[/b] to unravel the complex conspiracies on the ship if you want things to end well for Stella and the mission. That's right: Just like in Lacuna, the [b]story branches and ends based on your decisions and performance[/b] as an investigator.

The gameplay will feel familiar to fans of our first title: direct platformer-style controls, non-repeating branching dialogs, automatic saving (no going back!), collecting clues, submitting solutions to cases. However, we made some major improvements to the formula! In the next few paragraphs, we'd like to provide insights into our thinking behind some aspects of Between Horizons. If you want more marketing speak instead (and of course add the game to your wishlist <3), just check out its [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1921980/Between_Horizons/]store page[/url]!

[h2]Refined Detective Gameplay[/h2]

At its very core, Between Horizons is a detective game. We learned a lot about investigation mechanics while working on Lacuna, and we kept around some of the things that worked well:

[list]
[*] Cases are solved by filling in gaps in case sheets: you must complete sentences using names of people, places, and other clues you found.
[*] You can always drive the plot forward by submitting a case, even if your solution is wrong. If that happens, you may not know until later, when the consequences manifest themselves.
[*] Instead of alternating cutscenes with self-contained mini games, all the puzzles you solve are directly connected to what's happening in the story.
[/list]

Good detective games usually give the player a great amount of freedom to come up with the solution on their own. Hence, after a lot of trials and discussions, we landed on some improvements to the formula that aim to maximize player agency:

[list]
[*] You can submit the solution to a case at any point in time. You have to decide whether or not you know enough to crack it yet. This also makes it much easier to quickly replay content if you know the solution already.
[*] Any evidence you find (in the entire game!) can be assigned to any case (in the entire game!).
[*] Instead of being presented with a linear string of levels, you can freely move around parts of the ship to investigate. New areas unlock in a Metroidvania fashion as you progress through the story.
[*] You can present characters with evidence, and oftentimes you need to show someone the right clue to make them talk.
[/list]

[h2]Between The Lines[/h2]

Finally, Between Horizons is also very focused on its story, characters, and dialogs.

The idea for its premise originated back in 2020. We wanted to explore the concept of one generation setting out to do something and the next generation being presented with the consequences of that (unfinished) journey. We believe it's a relatable topic to many people especially nowadays, with the younger generation inheriting a host of different crises. The responsibility generations bear for one another is a complex and nuanced problem for which we believe to have found the perfect setting.

We can't wait to show you more of the game over the coming months. For now, we hope that you like what you see and that you enjoyed this little write-up of our thoughts behind the game. [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/38461427-DigiTales-Interactive/]Follow us on Steam[/url] for more updates and most importantly, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1921980/Between_Horizons/]add Between Horizons to your wishlist[/url]! Both would help us out a great deal.

Thanks a lot for reading, have a nice week!

Much love,
Everybody at DigiTales Interactive & Assemble Entertainment

notes.title: Let's party! Lacuna Anniversary Update now available!
notes.notes:
Hello, everyone!

Precisely a year ago, Lacuna launched on PC. It was DigiTales' first ever release, and we had no idea how it would go. Thankfully, its reception from both critics and players alike has been very positive. 

[h2]Thank you so much for your support, your reviews, appreciative messages, guides, achievement hunting, social media follows, and all the other nice things you've done as a community! It means the world to us.[/h2]

Today, we want to show our appreciation by bringing you [b]Community Items, Steam Deck support, and a big anniversary update[/b]!


[h2]Community Items[/h2]
We sat down and created some neat Steam Community Items for you to show off to your friends. Here's how they work in a nutshell: You earn Lacuna-themed trading cards by playing the game and by trading them on the community market with other players. Once your collection of six cards is complete, you can use them to craft a Lacuna-themed badge to show off on your Steam profile. Repeating the process levels up your badge to a maximum level of 5 (and there's a special foil badge you can earn by collecting all six rare foil cards). Crafting a badge also earns you additional Lacuna-themed random drops each time, like emojis and profile backgrounds.

[u][b]In a nutshell:[/b][/u]
[list]
[*] Collect the six trading cards representing some of Lacuna's main characters.
[*] Craft up to six badges to rise through the ranks at the CDI.
[*] Express yourself using the six new Lacuna emojis (including a super rare Horace)!
[*] Spice up your Steam profile using one of five Lacuna backgrounds.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38568502/ce230d16446ef6e97fa8c638581d21791fbd71e3.png[/img]

[h2]Steam Deck support[/h2]
Valve already rated Lacuna as "Playable" on Steam Deck a while ago, which is the second-best achievable rating. Having tested it ourselves, we can confirm that the game could already be played comfortably from start to finish on the Steam Deck. However, a mouse cursor would occasionally show up, which denied us the coveted "Deck Verified" rating. We have patched this and received the Verified rating just last night! It should become visible on Lacuna's page any moment now.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38568502/572304c6fc6bd280127b8377ee1b78c56b6b1b5c.jpg[/img]

[h2]Anniversary update[/h2]
Over the past year, we received a number of bug reports and other requests for improvements, the more severe of which we usually patched in right away. notes.title: Achievements Unlocked!
notes.notes:
Agents!

We are proud to announce that Lacuna 1.1.0 is now live. Among a number of [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1364100/discussions/1/3115906960353187466/]smaller fixes and improvements[/url], it brings you [b]achievements[/b]!

To be perfectly honest with you, we were so busy getting the game itself ready last month that the topic of achievements didn't really cross our minds. Due to popular demand, we prioritized adding them right after enabling cloud saves (and going on a short post-launch break).

Since this is an update for all you collectors out there, we should probably add that Steam Community Items (Trading Cards, Badges, and Store Points items) will also be added down the line, but aren't part of today's patch.

[h2]'Patchable' achievements[/h2]

We did our best to make each achievement patchable, i.e. automatically grant it to all players that met the requirements to receive it before this patch. This has been possible with most of them, but some track completely new variables – more on those below.

[b]To receive all patchable achievements you (would have) previously unlocked, please start the game and load each existing save file once.[/b] In other words: Click your previously used save slot(s) in the profile selection to be taken to the main menu, and you should receive everything you're owed at once. Let us know if you're not getting any achievements you feel like you should be.

[h2]'Non-patchable' achievements[/h2]

There is also a number of [b]non-patchable[/b] achievements. These can only be unlocked in a completely new save file – or in an ongoing one if you haven't played too far already:
[list]
[*][b]Happy Boi / Chonky Boi:[/b] you haven't beaten the first level where Neil appears as the protagonist.
[*][b]Good Cop / Bad Cop[/b]: you haven't finished the Villa level yet.
[*][b]She's Got A Point[/b]: you haven't had your second conversation with [spoiler]Zora[/spoiler] yet.
[*][b]Groupie:[/b] you haven't been down to Paluhn Market twice already.
[*][b]Consumer & Couch Potato:[/b] you haven't reached any of the game's finales yet.
[*][b]afk?[/b]: you haven't beaten the game yet.
[/list]
There are more plans, both Lacuna-related and otherwise, that we can't wait to share with you. Until then, we hope that you enjoy this first larger update!

Best wishes from DigiTales Interactive & Assemble Entertainment ❤️

notes.title: Thank You! || Cloud Saves Enabled || More Updates Soon
notes.notes:
Hey, everybody!

Lacuna came out last Thursday, and it's been quite the week for us here at DigiTales Interactive HQ (i.e. our respective apartments thanks to the pandemic). We want to thank you all so much for buying, playing, and reviewing the game. We did [b]not[/b] expect to hit 200 reviews at over 90% positive within eight days, and it's hard to overstate how happy it makes us that the game is being received so favorably.

That being said, after release is before release!

You guys have brought up some excellent points on how to improve the game. Based on your feedback, we have already been able to find and squash a number of bugs, and there are some more we have yet to take care of. You also asked for some additional features and QoL improvements, and we're happy to oblige.

Here's the plan:
[list]
[*] [b]Cloud saves[/b] are now enabled on Steam and GOG!
[*] The big update 1.1.0 is already in the works, but it won't be done before late June. Among other things, it will bring [b]achievements[/b] to Steam and GOG.
[*] We're releasing one minor update over the weekend, which fixes some small issues and adds a little bit of extra polish. We'll let you know all about it in the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1364100/discussions/1/3115906960353187466/]ongoing patch notes[/url] once it's out.
[/list]
There's some other things we've been looking into based on your feedback:
[list]
[*] We are going to allow players to set VO language and subtitles language separately. I cannot promise that this will be included in 1.1.0, but it's coming.
[*] Quite a few people have been asking if the [b]Lacuna soundtrack[/b] could be made available separately in some way. We've heard you and are working this out, but we have to ask for a little more patience.
[*] We are also working out if it could be possible to reload previous levels on a save file after beating the game once. More precisely, it would probably mean that you can reset the file to one of the story's three acts. This will be tricky to implement and take a while, but I already wanted to let you know we're trying to find a way!
[*] Lastly, a quick Q&A for recurring questions: 1. Lacuna: Prologue is the first few levels of Lacuna. Your saves transfer automatically. 2. Once the next small update is live, the dev team will go on its first short vacation for this year and will be back working on the game in mid June. Of course, we'll keep an eye on all the support channels and be here for you as usual the whole time.

Again, thank you all so much for your support!

Cheers,
[i]Julian (and greetings from everybody at DigiTales Interactive and Assemble Entertainment!)[/i]

notes.title: Lacuna coming to Steam 2021
notes.notes:
Lacuna is a story-based pixel art adventure in a beautiful 2D sci-fi “noir” universe, which challenges the player to utilize extensive dialogue options in order to make decisions with potentially serious consequences. In the game, players must use their moral compass to navigate an emotionally intense experience that may or may not stimulate some critical self-reflection. 
Additionally, the Noir-inspired pixel-art adventure game Lacuna, from DigiTales Interactive, won ‘Best Prototype’ at Game Award Saar.

[h2]Lacuna will be available on Windows PC via Steam in 2021. [/h2]
